data.narrative:
Tempo is a Series A climate and energy technology company that has raised $50M to date. The target operates in a sector with nine identifiable peers—one public (LNZA) and eight private companies including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix—though none provide sufficient comparable valuation data at the same stage and tier.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total raised ($50M) as a base proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A forward yields an implied valuation of $100M. This represents the most reliable signal available given the sparse comparable universe in the climate and energy sector at this stage. Peer-median analysis is not applicable; while eight same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparison simultaneously.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $85M to $115M, with a median of $100M. This range reflects reasonable variance around the stage-progression estimate but is supported by a single method, creating material reliance on the validity of the 2.0x multiplier assumption for Series A progression in this sector. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow peer comparables, Tempo's position within the climate tech funding environment, and whether the $50M raised proxy appropriately reflects post-money valuation dynamics.
